Print a plot, skipping ones that were never built

Source: R/theme-and-save.R
ggprint_rawr.Rd

The print-time counterpart to ggsave_rawr(), so a report chunk can unconditionally request a plot's display even when it was conditionally skipped upstream. A bare symbol is looked up by name in the calling environment; any other expression (plots[[nm]], a computed plot) is evaluated and judged by its value, so NULL counts as "not generated".

Usage

ggprint_rawr(input, interactive = FALSE)

Arguments

input

The object to print. When it is a bare variable name, that name is used to check existence rather than the value.

interactive

Return the plot as an interactive plotly widget (plotly::ggplotly()) instead of a static ggplot. The report templates pass their InteractivePlots param here. Objects ggplotly() cannot convert (ggpubr composites, sequence logos, base-graphics heatmaps, objects that are already widgets) are returned unchanged, so a report never breaks for requesting interactivity.

Only use this from an ordinary chunk: an htmlwidget printed from inside a results='asis' loop needs an explicit tagList/knit_print dance to get its dependencies attached, and silently renders empty without it.

Value

The object, so a knitr chunk prints it; a plotly widget when interactive = TRUE and the plot can be converted; invisible NULL with a warning when it was never generated.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
ggprint_rawr(p_corr_log2area_all)
ggprint_rawr(p_pca_scores, interactive = TRUE)
} # }
